EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Middle East saw a significant escalation with Israel striking Hezbollah command centers in Beirut's Dahiyeh district, directly in response to Hezbollah's rocket fire on northern Israel. This attack follows explicit Iranian warnings against such a strike and comes amidst heightened tensions, including a deadly shooting attack in central Israel, for which Hamas claimed responsibility, and ongoing Israeli military operations in Gaza and southern Lebanon.

IRAN
Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman, Asma'eil Bakaii, stated that negotiations with the US are difficult due to "constantly shifting demands and contradictory statements," emphasizing the need for the US to recognize Iran's right to peaceful nuclear enrichment under the NPT. Bakaii also accused the US of violating the ceasefire agreement by attacking Iranian commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz and on the high seas, warning that Iran's armed forces are "determined to respond to any attack with full force." The US Central Command reported shooting down two Iranian "one-way attack drones" threatening maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran has reportedly begun charging ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz, with average fees of $1.5-2 million per vessel, accepting cash, goods, services, or cryptocurrency (Tether). A US-drafted resolution for the IAEA Board of Governors demands Iran provide "accurate information" on bombed nuclear sites and enriched uranium stockp, and "grant the agency without delay all necessary access." Reports from Reuters indicate the US is considering using blocked Iranian assets to compensate Gulf states affected by Iranian attacks. Internally, Iranian students protested against new exam laws and the war's impact on their education. Pakistan's Interior Minister, Mohsin Naqvi, delivered a "special message" from Pakistan's PM and Army Chief to Ayatollah Seyyed Mojtaba Khamenei, with one source suggesting it concerned US agreement to ease sanctions on Tehran. An unconfirmed report by Fars News agency reported a "strong explosion" in Kharg, later clarified by the IRGC Navy as controlled demolition of old ammunition in the Bahregan area.

ISRAEL
Israel conducted airstrikes on Hezbollah command centers and infrastructure in Beirut's Dahiyeh district, responding to earlier rocket fire from Lebanon. Prime Minister Netanyahu and Defense Minister Katz confirmed the strike, with a senior Israeli official stating it aimed to "establish the equation we set." The US was reportedly informed in advance of the Dahiyeh operation. IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir visited the Gaza Strip, reiterating the objective to "disarm Hamas" and stating the IDF controls 60% of the Gaza Strip, soon to reach 70%. Zamir also approved plans to "further deepen the blow to Hezbollah" in Lebanon and vowed to "eliminate any organization of terrorists" in the West Bank. In central Israel, a shooting attack in the Kochav Ya'ir area resulted in one Israeli civilian killed (a 31-year-old man near Tzur Natan) and six injured (including a man in his 50s seriously wounded, a man in his 30s moderately, a woman aged 61 and a man aged 31 moderately). The perpetrator, Omar Yassin (21) from Tayibe, was identified as having a criminal record and was neutralized. Hamas claimed responsibility for the attack. In legal developments, the High Court of Justice ruled that Justice Minister Levin must cooperate with Supreme Court President Yitzhak Amit, following Levin's attempt to challenge Amit's appointment. Fifty-two individuals were arrested for participating in "riots" outside the home of Supreme Court Deputy President Noam Solberg. A government ministry CEO, Yehuda Avidan (identified with Shas), and two other senior officials are under investigation by Lahav 433 for fraud, breach of trust, abuse of power, and threats.

GAZA & WEST BANK
In Gaza, IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir stated the military continues to "erode Hamas's power" and aims for disarmament. The IDF and Shin Bet announced the killing of Sakr Abu Karim, a Hamas Nukhba Force commander and leader of the October 7 Kissufim raid, in a strike last week. Another Hamas cell commander, Muhanad Othman Yassin Farwana, was killed in an airstrike in southern Gaza overnight, accused of advancing terror plans. Al-Aqsa Hospital's ICU is reportedly bracing for a power outage due to dwindling fuel supplies. In the West Bank, Israeli settlers blocked Palestinian cars and hurled stones at the Efrat Junction, lightly injuring an Israeli civilian by a Palestinian driver who was later arrested. In Huwara, an IDF soldier was captured on video repeatedly punching a Palestinian man amidst clashes between Israeli civilians and Palestinians, prompting the IDF to condemn the soldier's actions and announce disciplinary proceedings. Nine Palestinians were reportedly wounded in the settler attack. Israeli forces abducted a Palestinian political science professor in Al-Khalil during a midnight raid. Palestinian officials reported over 1,600 attacks by Israeli forces and settlers against Palestinian civilians in the West Bank during May. Hamas claimed responsibility for the Kochav Ya'ir shooting attack, stating it was in response to "ongoing aggression in Gaza and crimes of Judaization and settlement expansion."

LEBANON
Israel conducted airstrikes on Beirut's Dahiyeh district, targeting Hezbollah command centers and infrastructure, with Lebanese media reporting two apartments hit by three missiles and multiple casualties. Civilian evacuations from Dahiyeh were reported. Hezbollah sources and Iranian officials (Araghchi) had previously threatened a "strong response" to any attack on Dahiyeh. Hezbollah's media-affiliated analyst Khalil Nasrallah indicated the group had not committed to avoiding strikes on northern Israeli settlements. The IDF issued an evacuation warning for Tyre and surrounding refugee camps, instructing residents to move north of the Zahrani River, citing "Hezbollah's violation of the ceasefire agreement." Israeli forces killed Cpt. Shahar Gamla (23) of the Egoz Unit, who succumbed to wounds from a Hezbollah drone attack late Thursday. Sgt. Ohad Yaari (21) of the Givati Brigade was killed Friday by a suspected accidental firearm discharge. Over the weekend, the IDF struck approximately 150 Hezbollah infrastructure sites in southern Lebanon, including weapon depots, command centers, and rocket launchers. Israeli airstrikes were also reported in al-Zarraria, Bousaliya, Nabatieh, and a vehicle in Maarakeh. Hezbollah launched two rockets at northern Israel (Yiftah and Ramot Naftali) which were intercepted, and an explosive-laden FPV drone wounded four IDF reservists moderately. An apparent Hezbollah drone struck near IDF forces in southern Lebanon, causing no injuries.

SYRIA & IRAQ
In Iraq, explosions were heard in Erbil Province, attributed to a landmine near Bradost (injuring one) and potentially related to attacks on Iranian anti-Iran Kurdish group PJAK's headquarters. PJAK claimed its headquarters were attacked by Iranian drones in Iraq. In Ba'aj, Ninawa province, PKK-affiliated gunmen reportedly killed a former PKK member. The US reportedly intercepted a drone over a "dissident freedom party stronghold" in Soran, Erbil province. In Syria, clashes were reported between "Golan elements" and drivers protesting the entry of Jordanian trucks and cars into Syrian territory.

GULF STATES
OPEC+ countries (including Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria, and Oman) announced adjustments to oil production, reaffirming commitment to market stability and a "cautious approach." Reuters reported that OPEC+ members are expected to agree on a fourth increase in oil output targets. The US is reportedly considering using blocked Iranian assets to help Gulf states (Kuwait and Bahrain) recover from damage caused by Iranian missile and drone attacks.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Dahiyeh Airstrikes:** Israel struck Hezbollah command centers and infrastructure in Beirut's Dahiyeh district in response to Hezbollah rocket fire.
2.  **Kochav Ya'ir Attack:** A shooting attack in central Israel resulted in one civilian killed and six injured, with Hamas claiming responsibility. The perpetrator, Omar Yassin, was neutralized.
3.  **Tyre Evacuation Warning:** The IDF issued an evacuation warning for the Lebanese city of Tyre and surrounding areas due to alleged ceasefire violations by Hezbollah.
4.  **IDF Casualties in Lebanon:** Cpt. Shahar Gamla was killed by a Hezbollah drone, and Sgt. Ohad Yaari died from an accidental firearm discharge, both in southern Lebanon.
5.  **IAEA Resolution on Iran:** The US drafted a resolution demanding Iran provide accurate nuclear information and full access to IAEA inspectors.
6.  **Strait of Hormuz Tensions:** The US shot down two Iranian drones threatening maritime traffic, while Iran claims control over the strait and is reportedly charging transit fees.
7.  **Israeli Espionage Concerns:** US media reported increased Israeli spying on US officials involved in Iran talks, with the Pentagon raising its counterintelligence threat level for Israel.
8.  **Settler Violence in West Bank:** Incidents of settler violence against Palestinians were reported in Efrat Junction and Huwara, including an IDF soldier assaulting a Palestinian, prompting official condemnation.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks are high following the Israeli strike on Dahiyeh, given explicit Iranian and Hezbollah threats of a "strong response." The fragile ceasefire in Lebanon is deeply strained, with the IDF's evacuation warning for Tyre indicating potential for further intensified operations. Active flashpoints include the Israel-Lebanon border, the West Bank (due to settler violence and recent attacks), and the Strait of Hormuz where direct US-Iran confrontations (drone interceptions, Iran's transit charges) continue. Military postures are hardening, with IDF Chief of Staff Zamir approving plans to "further deepen the blow to Hezbollah" and Iran reiterating its readiness to respond with "full force." Israel's red line on preventing Hezbollah fire on its territory has been reasserted by PM Netanyahu, while Iran considers US actions in Hormuz as ceasefire violations and a direct threat.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **US** was informed by Israel prior to the Dahiyeh strike. The US is drafting an IAEA resolution demanding transparency from Iran on its nuclear program. The US is also reportedly considering using blocked Iranian assets to compensate Gulf states for past damages. Former US President Trump, in an interview, stated he would not unfreeze Iranian assets or ease sanctions in any deal, and believes the UN could facilitate the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. **Pakistan**'s Interior Minister delivered a "special message" to Iran's Leader's aide, with some speculation it pertains to US sanctions relief. In **Europe**, France is leading efforts with Britain and Norway to impose national-level sanctions against Israeli individuals involved in West Bank violence, due to a lack of full EU consensus. **OPEC+** nations, including Saudi Arabia and other Gulf states, announced oil production adjustments, emphasizing market stability.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
There are contradictions regarding the number of perpetrators in the Kochav Ya'ir attack: the IDF initially reported two terrorists, one killed near Tzur Yitzhak and a second fleeing and later killed near Tayibe, while police later stated only one terrorist carried out the attack. Iran's Foreign Ministry claims the US is violating the ceasefire through actions in the Strait of Hormuz, while the US accuses Iran of threatening maritime traffic. Claims by Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Bakaii about "constantly shifting demands" in negotiations with the US are difficult to verify without more context on the negotiation specifics. Omid Dana, an Iranian opposition figure, consistently posts pro-Israel and anti-Iran regime content, which should be viewed through the lens of propaganda, celebrating Israeli strikes and disparaging the Iranian leadership. Press TV, an Iranian state-affiliated outlet, frames all Iranian actions as defensive and righteous, and Israeli/US actions as aggressive and criminal, which is a clear propaganda indicator. There is a reporting gap regarding the specific casualties in the Dahiyeh strike, with sources only mentioning "casualties" or "injuries" without precise numbers or affiliations.
